newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Asian stocks mixed but Hong Kong hits record high.
newsitem.headline: Asian stocks mixed but Hong Kong hits record high.

text.p: Most Asian stock markets closed higher on Thursday led by Hong Kong which continued its march into record territory.
Hong Kong stocks closed above 13,000 points for the first time ever, driven by optimism about interest rates and the property market, analysts said.
The Hang Seng index closed 61.11 points higher, or 0.47 percent, at 13,004.80 after hitting a record intra-day high at 13,009.74.

Analysts said the market was led by large property counters. Wednesday's government land auction, in which a plot of land sold at a price well above expectations, had revived optimism about the property market.
Brokers said the U.S. Federal Reserve's decision on Wednesday to leave interest rates unchanged added to the positive sentiment.

"In the medium-to-long term, the market is still not expensive," said Peter So, deputy head of research at Schroder Securities. So said the market was likely to see further upside potential due to earnings upgrades triggered by strength in the property market and stronger retail sales.
Tokyo stocks ended slightly higher although many investors stayed on the sidelines as even a slew of corporate earnings results failed to spark interest, brokers said.
The key Nikkei 225 average gained 51.60 points, or 0.25 percent, to close at 21,031.04.

Brokers said Prime Minister Ryutaro Hashimoto's financial deregulation plan, released earlier this week, was welcomed by the market, but investors would wait until all the ministries involved implement his plan successfully.
Turnover was a thin 248 million shares, down from 314 million on Wednesday.
Singapore investors showed no such reticence, pushing shares sharply higher in heavy trading.

Dealers said sentiment was strong with gains seen in several heavyweight stocks as funds continued a recent buying spree. Though the economy remains sluggish, funds are said to be buying in anticipation of a recovery next year.
The key Straits Times Industrials index jumped 43.28 points or 2.02 percent to close at 2,189.76. Volume was a hectic 232.9 million shares.
Australian shares rose as gold and other metal sectors found plenty of buying support on the back of firmer metal prices.
The benchmark All Ordinaries index closed up 15.6 points or 0.66 percent at 2,362.5, just off an intra-day high of 2,365.4.
The Jakarta share index crossed the key 600-point resistance level at the close on the back of selective foreign buying of larger stocks, brokers said.
The main index rose 5.42 points, or 0.91 percent, to close at 600.91 points.
Foreign investors also buoyed Thai stocks by buying blue-chip finance and bank issues, brokers said. The SET index gained 11.11 points, or 1.13 percent, to close at 990.62.
Manila shares also closed higher despite a tentative start. The main index rose by 0.76 percent, or 23.32 points, to end at 3,072.81.

Brokers said the market positioned itself ahead of next week's expected announcement of robust third-quarter economic growth figures and the meeting later this month in the Philippines of the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation forum, which is expected to shed a favorable light on the country.
At 1115 GMT, the dollar was trading at 111.62/1.72 yen and 1.5055/60 marks.
Gold prices ended lower in Hong Kong in lacklustre trade. Bullion closed at US$380.00/50 an ounce against New York's Wendesday close at US$383.05/45.
The SIMEX December contract for Brent crude rose to $24.00 per barrel, up 11 cents from Wednesday's close in London. The January contract last traded $23.54, up 20 cents from Wednesday.
